starting_conditions.defense: Warned, Tarawa-informed lagoon-side/local-sector defense with distributed ammunition, alternate command and surviving local mortar/direct-fire positions, but heavily suppressed and without meaningful depth.
starting_conditions.armor: Roi 0 traced Japanese combat tanks; Namur 0-1 contact-capable Type 94 tankette at dawn.
starting_conditions.terrain: Roi remains open/airfield-dominated; Namur remains more obstructed by vegetation, structures, debris and prepared strongpoints.
starting_conditions.US: 4th Marine Division assault supported by LVT/LVT(A), close destroyer/fire-support craft, artillery from preliminary islets, CVE support and tank elements.

landing_and_reduction.Roi: Repeated bombardment suppresses most exposed guns. A limited set of remanned weapons and mortars fires after lift, causing real LVT/infantry losses, but open terrain permits rapid spotting and direct suppression.
landing_and_reduction.Namur: More surviving protected positions reopen after the fire lifts. Lagoon-side fires and pre-registered mortar lanes produce greater friction than on Roi; LVT waves remain intact enough to establish a beachhead.
landing_and_reduction.traffic: Extra tractor/fire-support redundancy prevents a Tarawa-like failure, but lagoon/LST/LCI sequencing produces local 15-30 minute delays and wave intermixing rather than linear benefit from added craft.

landing_and_reduction.Roi: Tank/direct-fire/engineer reduction advances quickly across the exposed airfield. Organized resistance collapses late afternoon centered; isolated shelters continue firing intermittently.
landing_and_reduction.Namur: Advance is slower. Marine tanks, armored amtracs, engineers and direct gunfire reduce strongpoints sequentially; defenders use local sectors rather than a single mass counterattack.
landing_and_reduction.Type94: If the high case hull is operational, it functions briefly as a mobile/static machine-gun point and is destroyed/abandoned by early-to-mid afternoon centered. Contact-capable at T24 = 0.

landing_and_reduction.Roi: Mopping and isolation of small pockets.
landing_and_reduction.Namur: US line stabilizes before the remaining northern/eastern strongpoints. Small infiltration/local counterattack groups probe gaps; main 6/7-Feb night outcome remains open for next adjudication.

munition_secondary_explosion.branch_reason: Distributed ammunition, smaller protected magazines and blast separation reduce the probability that one demolition charge reaches a single bulk torpedo-warhead/aviation-ordnance concentration.
munition_secondary_explosion.centerline: One or more local ammunition secondary explosions occur, but no island-shaking magazine catastrophe comparable to the historical 20 killed/100 wounded event is centered.
munition_secondary_explosion.delay: Localized 15-35 minute disruption rather than a sector-wide long pause.

Japan_T24.Roi: Organized resistance broken; roughly 80-160 isolated/local fighters remain in pockets at T24.

assessment: Branch defense is visibly harder on Namur, but Roi's openness and US firepower cap the gain. Ammunition-dispersion improvements also remove a major historical correlated-loss mechanism for the Marines, preventing a one-directional casualty multiplier.
